title: Pending tool captures must expire and never lock out sessions
body: A pre-tool capture waits for the matching post-tool event, but that event is not guaranteed: Claude reports failed calls through PostToolUseFailure rather than PostToolUse, and denied or interrupted calls report nothing. Treating unfinished calls as protected state leaked one entry per failed or denied call; sessions holding any entry were never evicted, so after about a month every new session failed at the 128-session cap, and copied decision evidence in Stop review pending entries pushed state.json past its 10 MiB write limit. Rules: map PostToolUseFailure to after_tool; drop pending captures when the turn ends (Stop) and after 24 idle hours; bound pending entries per session; evict sessions least recently used regardless of pending entries, never the active one; write the state compactly and evict sessions rather than fail when it would exceed the store limit, reading oversized files so they can be shrunk. A dropped capture loses no evidence: a later post-tool event without it records a coverage gap, and drift is still computed from current captures. An attempt still in flight must not make status unavailable. Tentative: Stop review pending entries still copy all decision evidence per call; storing it once by digest was suggested but not implemented.

sources.note: 128 sessions with 684 leaked pending entries disabled hooks in new sessions; follow-up comments report status masking by in-flight attempts and state.json passing 10 MiB from duplicated Stop review evidence.
PostToolUse fires after success and PostToolUseFailure after a failed call; permission-rule denials and interrupts are not documented as firing a post-tool hook.
